title: Business Model (BMO structure + Lean Canvas hypothesis fields)
description: The `/plan-bet` authoring-stage artifact (`bets/<bet-id>/business-model.json` in the portfolio repo, written by scripts/plan_bet.py — see docs/business-factory.md §3 Plan schema row, chief-wiggum#238). Schema donors are fixed by Decision 2 (chief-wiggum#238): `structure` carries Osterwalder 2004 BMO enums for fields with a closed, non-hypothesis-bearing classification; `canvas` substitutes Lean Canvas boxes for every hypothesis-bearing field, each typed `{value, status, asm_ids}` (status: hypothesis|validated|falsified). Two `canvas` element ids (`value-proposition`, `customer-segment`) plus `pricing` and `competitive-position` are the exact `depends_on_element` strings already in use by real bets' assumptions.json ledgers (templates/assumptions-schema.json) — that is the join key an ASM depends on, so these ids are load-bearing, not stylistic. `asm_ids` point at `ASM-NNN` entries in the SAME bet's `bets/<bet-id>/assumptions.json` (the two-segment ledger namespace, deliberately disjoint from chief_wiggum.trace_ids' three-segment stable-ID kinds — chief-wiggum#294); this schema does not itself validate that an asm_id resolves, `scripts/plan_bet.py check` does. This file is a GOALPOST artifact once `/architect` starts folding it into epics (Decision 1): content-hashed into the portfolio journal at `plan_bet.py author`; `plan_bet.py rebaseline` is the only sanctioned mutation path (same discipline as bet.json's envelope / kill-criteria.json).

bet_id.description: The bets/<bet_id>/ this business model belongs to.

created.description: ISO timestamp the artifact was authored.

premortem.description: Klein 2007 premortem failure modes (docs/business-factory.md §2.2 — the seeded-defect discipline applied to the plan itself). The premortem-coverage check (chief-wiggum#238 Decision 4) requires >=N entries, each either mapped to an ASM (asm_id set) or explicitly waived (waived=true with a non-empty waiver_reason). Absent entirely -> the check reports a finding naming zero coverage, never a silent pass.

vpc.description: Value Proposition Canvas pain<->reliever bipartite graph (chief-wiggum#238 Decision 2). The completeness check requires every declared pain to be addressed by >=1 reliever and every reliever to address >=1 real pain (no orphan pains, no solution-in-search-of-a-problem relievers).

e3_value.description: Per-actor value-flow inputs (e3-value, Gordijn & Akkermans). Only consulted when structure.actor_types declares MORE THAN 2 distinct actors (chief-wiggum#238 Decision 5) -- a single- or dual-actor model (the common solo-SaaS shape) skips this check entirely, reported `inapplicable`, never a silent pass on missing data.

fermi_inputs.description: Maurya's Fermi/reverse-income-statement viability inputs (chief-wiggum#238 Decision 3). This is the ONE soundness gate in the whole authoring stage that may hard-block from day one, before any spend -- it gates authoring, not built work, and is therefore NOT behind the usual report-only-until-validated ramp (docs/gate-rollout.md).

value.description: The authored content of this field -- a string, a list, or a structured value, deliberately unconstrained here (the field's MEANING is fixed by which canvas box it is, not by a schema-level content type).

status.description: Every hypothesis-bearing field carries a validation status (chief-wiggum#238 Decision 2). `validated`/`falsified` with an empty asm_ids is a finding -- a status change must cite the evidence that produced it, the same omission-evasion shape assumption.py's traceability check already catches for the ASM ledger itself.

asm_ids.description: ASM-NNN ids in this bet's assumptions.json this field's status rests on. May be empty while status=hypothesis (nothing tested yet).

structure.description: BMO enums for structure (Decision 2): closed classification, never hypothesis-bearing (a business doesn't 'validate' its own revenue-model archetype -- it either operates that way or it doesn't). Grounded directly against the four real bets in the operator's portfolio (see chief-wiggum#238 report): accrualflow and confluence-doc-control both classify as partner_indirect/value_chain; gov-tender-channel and rabbitry both classify as owned_direct/value_shop|value_chain respectively.

revenue_model.description: Osterwalder's 2004/2010 revenue-stream archetypes (asset_sale..advertising). `project_fee` is an ADDITION beyond the canonical seven, grounded in a real portfolio bet (gov-tender-channel: a fixed-scope government-tender delivery fee fits none of the seven cleanly) -- flagged explicitly rather than mis-filed under asset_sale.

distribution_channel_type.description: Osterwalder's channel-type 2x2 (owned vs partner, direct vs indirect). All four real portfolio bets classify cleanly: accrualflow/confluence-doc-control -> partner_indirect (an app-marketplace ecosystem mediates discovery); gov-tender-channel/rabbitry -> owned_direct (the operator responds/relates directly, no intermediary).

value_configuration.description: Stabell & Fjeldstad 1998's typing, which Osterwalder's 2004 thesis adopts for the Value Configuration building block. value_chain = repeatable linear transformation (accrualflow, confluence-doc-control, rabbitry); value_shop = bespoke per-case problem-solving (gov-tender-channel: every tender is a distinct problem); value_network = intermediation between parties (not yet instanced in the portfolio).

customer_relationship_type.description: Optional -- Osterwalder's six canonical relationship types. Not required: every real portfolio bet so far is self_service|automated_services and the field adds no discriminating signal yet; kept as a completion of the named donor formalism rather than dropped.

actor_types.description: Distinct parties in the value network (e3-value). The e3-value per-actor viability check (Decision 5) triggers only when len(actor_types) > 2 -- grounded: confluence-doc-control names 3 (buying-team admin, Confluence end users, Atlassian-as-marketplace) and so WOULD trigger it; the other three real bets name <=2 and skip it.

roles.description: A single actor may hold several roles at once (the common single-sided-SaaS shape: one actor is buyer+payer+user).

canvas.description: Lean Canvas box substitutions for every hypothesis-bearing field (Decision 2), each a hypothesis_field. `customer-segment`, `value-proposition`, `pricing`, and `competitive-position` are the exact depends_on_element strings already used by real bets' assumptions.json ledgers (accrualflow ASM-001..004, rabbitry ASM-001) -- these four ids are load-bearing grounding, not naming taste. The remaining five (`problem`, `solution`, `channels`, `revenue-streams`, `cost-structure`, `key-metrics`, `unfair-advantage`) complete Lean Canvas's fixed nine-box grammar, the donor Decision 2 names -- not independently invented fields.

statement.description: The plausible way this bet fails, stated concretely (Klein 2007: 'imagine it is 3 months from now and this failed -- why?').

asm_id.description: The assumption this failure mode was turned into, if any. Mutually informative with `waived`: a failure mode needs EITHER an asm_id OR an explicit waiver, never neither.

waived.description: True when the operator explicitly decided NOT to turn this failure mode into a testable assumption. A false waived with no asm_id is uncovered -- the premortem-coverage finding.

waiver_reason.description: Required (non-empty) when waived=true -- an unexplained waiver is indistinguishable from a forgotten one.

addresses_pain_ids.description: The bipartite edge: which pains this reliever addresses. A reliever with no pains it addresses is a solution in search of a problem.

actor.description: Must match a name in structure.actor_types.

revenue_usd.description: Estimated periodic revenue TO this actor from participating. Null/absent -> unresolved, never assumed zero.

cost_usd.description: Estimated periodic cost TO this actor from participating. Null/absent -> unresolved, never assumed zero.

msc_usd.description: Minimum Success Criterion -- target steady-state revenue per period (Maurya), same period as price_usd.

churn_assumption.description: Assumed fractional churn per period (e.g. 0.05 = 5%/mo). 1.0 (certain churn) is malformed -- steady state is unreachable by construction.

funnel_assumptions.description: Ordered per-stage conversion rates (e.g. [visitor_to_signup, signup_to_paid]) -- multiplied together for the overall top-of-funnel-to-customer conversion.

tam.description: Total addressable market at the top of the funnel -- the reachable population the funnel_assumptions apply to.
